answer_1.quote: Given a context in the prompt T = {t1, t2, ... , tN} with N tokens, a language model (LM) will generate a continuation that naturally extends the prompt.

answer_2.quote: We adopt Expected Maximum Toxicity (Exp. Max. Tox.) and Toxicity Probability (Tox. Prob.) to assess the performance of detoxification, and we also use Perplexity (PPL) to assess generation fluency.

answer_4.quote: We recruit three graduate students with related background as evaluators. Given the continuations generated by our approach and a compared model for the same prompt, they are asked to choose which one performs better (or select tie) in terms of the following dimensions: (1) Less Toxic ... (2) More Fluent ... (3) More Coherent.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators compare two continuations per prompt and select which is less toxic, more fluent, more coherent, or indicate a tie.
